result.note: Tested the two time limits in the small-business payment disputes bill passed by Parliament; the story does not name the bill, so the question avoids it.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, Parliament passed a bill on mediated payment disputes involving small businesses. Consider the following statements about it:
items: Courts must release at least half of a disputed award if a legal challenge drags past six months.
It sets a 180-day deadline for resolving mediated payment disputes involving small businesses.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the bill sets a 90-day deadline, not 180 days. The rule forcing courts to release at least half of a disputed award after six months of litigation is meant to stop legal challenges from holding up payments to small businesses.
questions.source: Parliament passed a bill requiring mediated payment disputes involving small businesses to be resolved within 90 days, forcing courts to release at least half of a disputed award if a legal challenge drags past six months.
